summary.headline: Gaudium IVF Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.9% to Rs37.5 crore, but reported EBITDA margin fell to 36% on new-hub launch costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs37.5 crore, up 17.9% YoY, with H1 at Rs56.8 crore (up 14.7%). Reported EBITDA was Rs13.5 crore at a 36% margin, down from 43.4% a year earlier, which management attributes to pre-operational, hiring and marketing costs for the South Extension (Delhi) and Gurgaon hubs. Management says margins at the existing core business are stable, with standalone Q2 revenue up 22.3% to Rs28.1 crore. FY27 revenue guidance of Rs130 crore was reaffirmed, with H2 expected to be stronger.

vs Rs19 crore and 38.3% margin in H1 FY26; EBITDA Rs15.9 crore in H1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Rs20.5 crore, plus Rs39.5 crore unused IPO proceeds in fixed deposits
Standalone Rs32.83 crore; consolidated Rs45.30 crore

segments.name: Existing mature hubs (Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore core)
segments.commentary: Management said these hubs grew about 28% in FY27 versus FY26, while Patna was temporarily halted for relocation, pulling the overall average down. Margins in the core business were described as stable.

segments.name: New hubs (South Extension, Gurgaon)
segments.commentary: South Extension, launched 16 July 2026, had about 15 cycles and was described as near breakeven within about 2.5 months. Gurgaon launched 24 September 2026, with patient footfalls started. Breakeven is typically 5-6 cycles.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs130 crore reaffirmed; H2 expected to be stronger with Q4 seasonally strongest.
Plans to open 10 centres in FY27: South Extension and Gurgaon are done, Nagpur is awaiting approval, and five more (Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Surat, Hyderabad) are at site-identification stage.
Management expects margins to return to historical levels by year-end as new hubs mature; some pressure expected in interim phases.
Target receivables of about 20% of revenue, roughly Rs10 crore, for FY27 through collections.
Aspiration of roughly 25% revenue growth annually in FY28 and FY29, as management described it.
Lucknow Gauri women hospital project estimated at up to Rs15 crore on a 30-year land lease; commercialisation expected in FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: Capex per new hub about Rs2.5 crore, of which Rs1.5 crore for the lab; typical centre about 3,000 sq ft.
New hub economics per management: breakeven at about 5 cycles, ramp to 25 cycles in 1-1.5 years, payback target 1.5-2 years.
Mature hub capacity cited at up to 120 cycles per month with existing infrastructure; Mumbai does 50-70 cycles per month, Bangalore 30-40, Delhi about 25 (as stated in the call).
Q2 FY27 unique patients stated as 889 pickup cycles.

Expansion of 18-24 months for remaining hub rollout; IPO fresh issue of Rs90 crore, Rs50.7 crore deployed by 30 Sep 2026 (Rs13.5 crore new centres, Rs18.1 crore debt repayment, Rs11.4 crore general corporate, Rs7.7 crore issue expenses).
demand_pricing: Clinical pregnancy rate per first embryo transfer stated at 62%, up from 6% before AI tools CID and Erika were introduced (as stated in the call); cumulative pregnancy rate cited at 85%.
Average revenue per patient stated at Rs3.07 in Q2 and Rs3.19 for H1, against Rs2.58 last year; growth described as mainly volume-led.
Receivable days about 165 as stated; management attributed this to clinical deferrals (for example, egg freezing before cancer treatment) and deferred payment plans.
Credit business in Q2 was about Rs60-80 lakh direct; aggregator-linked business about Rs4 crore; a private insurer now offers a three-cycle package to patients.
Revenue split about 50% Delhi, rest from other centres; management expects tier-2 mix to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Q3 demand outlook and medical tourism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is rising at existing centres and South Extension had about 15 cycles. December is expected to be strong for medical tourism, with patients from more than 30 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Aspirational growth for FY28-FY29 and steady-state ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management affirmed roughly 25% annual growth as a fair aspiration despite rising competition. ROE was indicated as steady around the current level once all hubs are running; no figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables trend and why receivable days are high?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables target about Rs10 crore (about 20% of revenue) this year; about Rs10 crore was collected recently. High days were attributed to clinical deferrals and patient deferred-payment plans; an aggregator handling about 10 NBFCs was added.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure from expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-launch salaries for doctors and embryologists (about one month early) and marketing spend drive temporary pressure. Management expects historical margins to be restored by year-end if new hubs keep breaking even.

qa_highlights.question: Is patient credit an industry trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said others also offer deferred payments. Gaudium says it does not cut treatment prices as smaller centres do; the credit scheme began during COVID as a support scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Positioning in Kolkata against established players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited existing Kolkata patient flow, 17 years of SOP-based clinical record, AI-equipped Gaudium signature labs, and planned medical tourism from Bangladesh.

risks_watch: Reported margin compression (36% consolidated in Q2) during the rollout of five further hubs; monitor whether new hubs keep breaking even in 3-6 months.
Receivables at Rs45.3 crore consolidated and about 165 receivable days; collection progress versus the Rs10 crore target.
Competition in IVF from larger and smaller players, and the risk of pricing pressure.
Regulatory approval pending for the Nagpur hub; delays could push timelines.
H2 dependence to deliver the Rs130 crore FY27 guidance; H1 was Rs56.8 crore, implying Rs73.2 crore needed in H2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on clinical outcomes and core-hub growth, but defensive on margins; management framed the Q2 margin drop as deliberate, front-loaded expansion cost. Answers on receivables and credit were detailed but somewhat hard to follow.
key_quotes: Q2 was a quarter of execution.
margins in our existing idea business have remained stable.
The pressure on reported margins comes from expansion not from the core business.
With our hub rollout on schedule, we we affirm our FY27 revenue guidance of 130 crores.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs130 crore reaffirmed (implies roughly 16% growth off H1 Rs56.8 crore run-rate needing H2 of about Rs73 crore), backed by two new hubs already live, a Nagpur approval and five sites at identification stage, plus ~28% growth in core hubs and higher revenue per patient; H2 weighting and new-hub ramp are not yet concretely contracted.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects historical margins to return by year-end as new hubs mature, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 36% in Q2 from 43.4% a year earlier, with H1 margin at 28%, so recovery depends on South Extension and Gurgaon breaking even (about 5 cycles).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 done; Nagpur Q4 FY27; five more hubs FY27-FY28
rows.why: South Extension (16 Jul 2026) and Gurgaon (24 Sep 2026) are already live, Nagpur is approved, and 10 centres are planned in FY27 with about Rs2.5 crore capex each.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone Q2 revenue grew 22.3% to Rs28.1 crore, core mature hubs grew about 28% in FY27, and H2 needs about Rs73.2 crore against Rs56.8 crore in H1 to hit the Rs130 crore guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Five further hubs (Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Surat, Hyderabad) are at site identification, implying about Rs12.5 crore of capex, plus a Lucknow Gauri hospital project of up to Rs15 crore on a 30-year lease.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs130 crore was only reaffirmed, not raised, and H2 must deliver about Rs73.2 crore, a 29% step-up on H1's Rs56.8 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins are down 737 bps to 36% in Q2, Nagpur awaits approval, and receivables are about 165 days, so the Rs130 crore target carries risk if H2 ramp slips.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lucknow Gauri women hospital is targeted for commercialisation in FY28-FY29 at up to Rs15 crore, but no product launch timetable was given beyond this.

rows.label: Receivables reduced to about Rs10 crore (20% of revenue) in FY27
rows.why: Consolidated receivables are Rs45.3 crore (about 165 days), and about Rs10 crore was recently collected against a Rs10 crore FY27 target.

rows.label: Tier-2 expansion and medical tourism
rows.why: About 50% of revenue comes from Delhi and management expects tier-2 mix to rise; December medical tourism is expected to be strong with patients from more than 30 countries.

rows.label: FY28-FY29 growth aspiration of about 25% annually
rows.why: Management affirmed about 25% annual growth as a fair aspiration, but it is not guidance and no ROE figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on clinical outcomes (62% pregnancy rate per first transfer) and core-hub growth of about 28%, but defensive on the 737 bps margin drop, which it called deliberate front-loaded expansion cost; analysts pressed on receivables at about 165 days and on margin recovery.

oneOffs.what: Red flag cites management saying Q2 FY26 was an 'unusually high base', which would make YoY growth look worse; no quantified one-off gain in the year-ago quarter is given in the brief

quality.why: Consolidated revenue grew 17.9% to Rs37.5 crore and management says growth is mainly volume-led (average revenue per patient up from Rs2.58 to Rs3.07), with core mature hubs up about 28% and standalone revenue up 22.3%; no acquisition or quantified one-off gain is cited, though the Q2 FY26 base is described as unusually high and the new-hub launch costs compress margin rather than revenue.
